_comment: PLAT-35 — THE TIER-4 READINGS OF THE GPUI FRONT-END'S OWN FRAMES.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM `tier4-review.json`, SAID FIRST BECAUSE
THE SPLIT IS THE DECISION MOST LIKELY TO BE READ AS EVASION.
`tier4-review.json` is the gated deliverable: the suite refuses it four
ways and a reading scoring below 4 BLOCKS unless it is in that file's
`knownRed` block, which asserts in both directions that the quarantined
set is EXACTLY the set scoring below 4. RE-COUNTED 2026-10-03, because
this paragraph was written over twelve readings and there are now
eighteen: TEN OF EIGHTEEN score below 4 — six of six in iteration 1, four
of six in iteration 2, and NONE in iteration 3. Putting them in `knownRed`
would still mean quarantining ten entries, and a quarantine
ledger holding ten of eighteen entries is not a quarantine — it is the gate
switched off while wearing the shape of a gate. So the SCORES here are
ungated, the findings are carried in PLAT-35's status with
owners, and `tier4-review.json` is left exactly as it was: six readings of
the ELECTRON arm, with its two quarantines.
THE SCORES ARE UNGATED. THE FILE IS NOT (added 2026-10-02).
`src/frontend/gpui/tests/test_plat35_ledger_integrity.nim` re-derives this
file's `gate` counts from its own `findings`, checks `gate.met` against
them in BOTH directions, requires a unique id, an owner, a closed-set
severity and substantial text on every finding, refuses a finding that is
both resolved and unresolved, and checks the reading population against
`scenarios.json` — count per iteration, each scenario once, and every
reading's view and viewport against that file's own tables. Until that
suite existed NOTHING in the tree read this file: `grep -rn` for its name
found it in prose only. An unread ledger's least reliable sentence is its
own summary, which is `Verification-Harness-Traps.md` 4; declining to gate
a SCORE is a decision, and leaving a record unread is not one.
WHAT THESE READINGS ARE OF. The frames of the GPUI front-end's own scene,
captured by `ci/test/plat35-gpui-capture.sh` through
`codetracer-gpui --pixels-out`. Before iteration 1 PLAT-35's GPUI arm was
the SHADOW TREE only (`PLAT35-VG1`), so no tier-4 reading of that
front-end existed to score.
THEY ARE AGENT READINGS, DECLARED AS SUCH, exactly as `tier4-review.json`
declares its six. There have been ZERO human reviews of the GPUI arm.
HOW TO READ THE RATINGS. The brief's own grammar makes below-4 a MISSING
OR DISTORTED ELEMENT rather than an aesthetic opinion. In iterations 1 and
2 every reading below 4 was there for one finding — the window drew no
debug-controls strip at all (`PLAT35-F1`). Iteration 3 is the first taken
AFTER upstream's chrome work and against the corpus's real 116-line
program, and `PLAT35-F1` is closed there, so iteration 3's numbers are not
comparable with iterations 1 and 2 as a trend: a different window, a
different recording and a different set of open findings.
THE GATE IS THE LEDGER AND NOT THE NUMBER. `findings` below is the
ledger; PLAT-35's status carries it with an owner per entry. Six P1 and
eight P2 entries are unresolved, so the gate is NOT met and the milestone
stays `partial`.

`recordingId:` printed. THIS IS THE ONE.
The recording command, verbatim, with that build:

CODETRACER_PYTHON_RECORDER_PATH="$REC/bin/codetracer-python-recorder" \
CODETRACER_PYTHON_INTERPRETER=/nix/store/65p6ipj712fb5igr9w1h5k5cb7bymj42-python3-3.12.13/bin/python3 \

`ct` was `src/build-debug-repro/bin/ct`, `CodeTracer version:
26.10.1(debug)`. The staging directory was then stamped
`.ctui-fixture-complete` and renamed to
`test-logs/tui-fixtures/calc-2f0db4f45192`, which is

capture lane and the TUI fixture provider both resolve it with no
environment override.
The recording carries one caveat, recorded rather than hidden: the
recorder printed `this trace is INCOMPLETE. 6 record(s) were discarded
because the Nim trace-writer backend did not persist them:
bind_variable=6`. Six bindings are missing from a 171-tick trace. No
iteration-3 finding depends on a bind_variable record.
WHAT THAT CAVEAT COSTS, MEASURED AT REVIEW 2026-10-03 rather than
left as a reassurance. The state pane lists only four of the
program's nine module-level names: `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div` are
there and `OPERATIONS`, `EXPRESSIONS`, `apply_op`, `evaluate` and
`main` are NOT, where the brief's own 2026-09-21 reading of a
complete recording names `EXPRESSIONS` and `OPERATIONS` as present.
The 'no finding depends on it' claim SURVIVES that — re-checked
entry by entry: F4's defect is the absence of a type field and of
any `data-column` attribute (structural, 0 in every scenario), F7's
is `__file__`'s elision (`__file__` is present), F11's is the C
comment around `mul` (present), VG8's is a node census; and F4's
secondary note that the pane shows the MODULE's names rather than
the frame's is the brief's own 2026-09-21 measurement and so
predates this fixture. But it is NOT true that the fixture is
equivalent to a complete recording, and the stamp cannot say so:
`fixture_provider.recordFixture` writes `.ctui-fixture-complete`
on `ct record` rc 0 alone and never parses the recorder's
INCOMPLETE line, so the provider would have stamped this same
directory. A later lane that needs every binding will therefore
ADOPT this one (`resolveFixture` hits the cache on stamp + a `.ct`)
and read five absent globals as a product defect. Nothing in the
tree asserts on those names today — `test_fixture_corpus.nim` has
no case over them — which is why this is recorded here instead of
being caught by a red lane. PROPOSED, not done: have
`recordFixture` refuse, or stamp differently, when `ct record`
prints `this trace is INCOMPLETE`.

findings.finding: the MARK has no reserved lane in the gutter. `gutterText` puts the padding IN FRONT of the lanes, so the lanes' cell indices move with the line number's digit count: on a one-digit row the mark occupies the same cell that a two-digit row's TENS DIGIT occupies, and the execution pointer occupies the cell that a two-digit row's MARK occupies. The dot therefore forms no column a reader (or PLAT-39's ink-cluster reader) can scan down.
findings.measurement: `leaves.gutterText` is `spaces(numberWidth - number.len) & pointerGlyph(row.pointer) & markGlyph(row.mark) & number & GutterGap` — unchanged in this rebase (`git log d34c6e087..HEAD -- src/frontend/gpui/app/leaves.nim` is empty). findings.cause: the padding precedes the lanes rather than separating them from the number. That is deliberate — `gutterText`'s own comment says it is so that `GutterGap` stays the only wide gap on a row, which is what PLAT-39's reader locates the gutter's end by — and this is its consequence. A fix reserves one cell per lane and pads between the lanes and the number, which moves every gutter x in every frame, so it is a capture-and-re-grade change rather than a one-line one.

gate.note: A numeric rating is a summary of this ledger and not a substitute for it. Iteration 3 is a RE-GRADE at 73e8c3dc4 against the corpus's real 116-line program and it moved the ledger in both directions: two P1 entries (F1, F6) and the capture-provenance entry (C1) closed on upstream work and a real recording, F9 was rewritten to the residue of a finding whose three measured halves closed, F10 was re-characterised, F14 stopped being an arithmetic claim, and ONE NEW ENTRY was opened (F17). FOURTEEN remain. THE COUNTS, AND THE ONE THE REVIEW MOVED: the re-grade filed F17 at P2 and published five P1 / nine P2; the review raised F17 to P1 (see its `severityRaisedAtReview`) because it is the still-failing half of the expected-elements clause F1 was a P1 for, so the published counts are SIX P1 and EIGHT P2. The total is fourteen either way and `met` is false either way — P1 and P2 block this gate identically — but a P1 count that falls because one clause was split across two owners is not progress, and it is not recorded as any. THE FRAMING FINDING, stated here because it is about the milestone and not about a frame, RE-PARTITIONED at review because the first version of this sentence added to fourteen while mis-sorting one entry: of the fourteen, FIVE are PLAT-35's to fix — F3 (jointly with PLAT35-PD1), F10, F11 (jointly with PLAT-42's OCR grammar, and blocked on a Wayland-only lane), F13, F14 — TWO are explicitly NOT GPUI-side (F8 is PLAT-45's, F17 is the shared mark set's and the design system's), and the remaining SEVEN are owned by PLAT-40 (F2, F4, F7), PLAT-41 (F5, F12), PLAT-47/PLAT-40 (F9) and PLAT-21/PLAT-3 (VG8). Of the six P1s, FIVE are not PLAT-35's to fix (F2, F4, F5, F7 and F17) and one is (F3). A gate worded as 'zero unresolved P1 and P2' over a ledger whose majority is other milestones' work is not reachable within PLAT-35 alone. These numbers are not only prose: `src/frontend/gpui/tests/test_plat35_ledger_integrity.nim` RE-DERIVES unresolvedP1 and unresolvedP2 from `findings` and checks `met` against them in both directions, so a count that drifts from its own ledger is a failing case rather than a sentence nobody reads. WHAT THAT SUITE DOES NOT GATE, found at review: it checks the shape of the UNRESOLVED set only. `resolved` entries are checked for nothing but id-disjointness — no owner, no closed-set severity, no text floor — so moving an entry from `findings` to `resolved` is the one edit that lowers both counts and reddens nothing. That is why F1 and F6 were re-measured here by hand rather than taken on the ledger's word.
gate.scoresVersusThisGrammar: RECORDED AT REVIEW, 2026-10-03, so the jump from 3/4 to 4-6 is not read as progress it has not earned. This file's own grammar says a reading below 4 is a MISSING OR DISTORTED ELEMENT. F17 is an unmet clause of the brief's `shell` expected-elements block and is listed against all six iteration-3 frames, so under that grammar every iteration-3 reading would be at or below 4; `shell` and `editorWithMark` are 6 and `eventLog` is 5. The readings are NOT re-scored here — a reading is what an agent said on a date, and rewriting one at review would destroy the only thing it is evidence of — but the scores are therefore not comparable with iterations 1 and 2 even within iteration 3's own frame, and the ledger below is the gate.
